subject: MAP & evaluation close: commits, true-up mechanics, and price protection

Subject: MAP and eval timeline — initial asks

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team is excited to move into an eval. We'd like to align the mutual action plan (MAP) and the commercial mechanics up front so procurement and legal have a clear close path. Key asks from BrightPay: 

- A 90-day evaluation with canary traffic and a pilot discount.
- A ramp schedule that ties committed spend to milestone discounts (Q1 ramp 25%, Q2 50%, Q3 full).
- Clear true-up cadence (BrightPay prefers annual true-ups, procurement is pushing for quarterly visibility).
- Price protection for at least 18 months post-close on the committed unit price.
- Definition of billable usage: does cached/intra-app inference count?

I've attached our internal MAP template and will share with legal. Can you confirm our proposed timeline: pilot starting 10/10, production ramp beginning 11/15, contract signing target 11/30? Also please send the commercial terms we would expect to see in an initial SOW.

Thanks,
Ellen Park
Head of AI Platforms
BrightPay

From: soojin.lee@redwood.ai

Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, connor.obrien@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-29T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP and eval timeline — initial asks

Ellen — really appreciate the clear timeline. Quoting your asks below and inline answers: 

> 90-day evaluation with canary traffic and a pilot discount.
We can do a 90-day eval with a canary route and token/embedding caps. Proposed pilot discount: 40% off hosted API rates for the eval period (limited to 1M tokens). If you want the dedicated pool for the pilot, we can quote that separately.

> Ramp schedule tied to committed spend and milestone discounts.
We propose a milestone waterfall tied to committed monthly spend: 0-3 months (pilot) = pilot pricing; months 4-6 = 30% discount on list for the committed baseline; months 7-12 = 15% discount as usage ramps to commit. We can translate into fixed commits if procurement prefers dollars rather than percentage.

> True-up cadence.
We usually do quarterly reporting with annual contractual true-up. For a commercial close we can accept quarterly invoice-level true-ups and an annual reconciliation to align committed vs actuals.

> Price protection for 18 months.
Our standard is 12 months price protection on committed unit pricing. Extending to 18 months is possible, but we'd need to tighten the true-up mechanics and commit levels. If BrightPay wants 18 months, we'd ask for a 10% increase in the baseline commit or a ramped minimum.

> Definition of billable usage (cached/intra-app inference).
Billable usage = tokens generated from live production API calls (inference requests that return tokens). We exclude local dev/sandbox environments under 10K tokens/month per seat. We count cache hits for prefix/KV cache as billable if they are served from our runtime (i.e., cache persisted on Redwood side) because that reduces marginal cost but still consumes runtime resources. If BrightPay insists on excluding cached responses, we'll need to disable Redwood-managed caching or provide a different pricing structure.

Attached is a draft MAP/SOW (Redwood_MAP_v2.docx) showing milestones and the commercial waterfall. Two asks from our side: (1) confirm whether procurement needs commits in dollars or tokens; (2) confirm if legal can accept 12-month price protection or requires 18 months.

Next step: Can we lock the pilot start for 10/10 and a sign-off call on 10/06?

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

Date: 2026-10-05T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: BrightPay redlines — negotiation playbook

Team — I reviewed BrightPay's redlines and procurement asks. Summary, risk, and recommended response below. Quoting the key external asks and our proposed stances: 

1) Price protection: BrightPay asking 18 months.
   - Risk: longer price protection increases exposure to hardware/ops cost inflation.
   - Proposal: offer 12 months price protection on committed unit pricing, with the option to extend to 18 months in exchange for a 12% uplift on baseline commit OR a guaranteed minimum ARR of $500k in year 1. Rationale: trade duration for economic certainty.

2) True-up cadence: they want quarterly true-ups + refund/credit on under-delivery.
   - Risk: quarterly true-ups are operationally fine; refund obligations are high risk.
   - Proposal: accept quarterly reporting and quarterly true-ups for visibility. For remediation, offer credit (not cash refund) applied to future invoices, with a cap equal to the quarterly commit shortfall. Add an annual reconciliation that settles net over/under-delivery.

3) Billable usage definition: exclude customer-managed cache hits.
   - Risk: if we exclude cache hits but still route work through our runtime, cost and billing alignment break.
   - Proposal: define billable usage precisely: 
     - Billable = tokens produced by Redwood runtime for API calls that return generated tokens. 
     - Exclude calls served entirely from customer-managed caches (explicitly controlled by BrightPay) provided they do not use Redwood-managed KV/prefix caches. 
     - If BrightPay wants Redwood-managed caching, it will be billable.

4) Unilateral price increase limitation for 24 months.
   - Proposal: accept limitation on unilateral increases for committed unit pricing tied to the agreed commit; allow indexing of non-committed list rates with 90-day notice.

Commercial offer to present to BrightPay on call: 
- Pilot: 90-day eval, 40% pilot discount, capped to 1M tokens.
- Commit schedule: sliding waterfall with minimum baseline commit $500k ARR for year 1 to unlock 18-month protection option (or 12% uplift alternative).
- True-ups: quarterly reporting + quarterly true-ups, remediation via credits, annual reconciliation.
- Billable usage: clear definition above; exclude customer-managed caches only.

Questions for Soojin/Connor/Rafael:
- Can we live with $500k baseline or do we need to push higher?
- Approve the credit (not cash) remediation approach?
- Approve the 12% uplift as the standard trade for 18-month protection?

If approved, I'll draft a redline response and a second MAP doc version that shows the commit/discount waterfall and the trade options. Recommend a call with Ellen + procurement on 10/07 to present the trade.

Neha Kapoor
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
